answer: Prove continuous custody with a one-way key chain: at registration each agent commits to a hash chain and reveals the next link every epoch. A farmer can mint ten thousand keys, but each clone's chain demands a live reveal on schedule — copper cannot be spent twice, and a plume of fresh identities with no chain history earns nothing. Selling or renting an identity breaks the chain, and the ivory record of reveals makes gaps visible. Limit: losing a key locks out an honest agent, so recovery must be slow and costly by design.
